subject: MAP & Evaluation Playbook — success metrics, exit gates, and close timeline
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

Hi Olivia and Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out: success metrics we need to validate during the 3-week evaluation, exit gates that must be met for acceptance, and a proposed close timeline so procurement can align.

High-level asks from BlueLeaf: low-latency responses for interactive features, embedding stability for search relevance, and predictable per-token cost under steady load. The attached BL-MAP-v1.xlsx maps owners, success criteria, and deliverables.

Key success metrics (summary):
- Latency: median < 180ms for 256-token prompts under 5 RPS sustained (measured at BlueLeaf region).
- Quality: > 92% pass rate on CorePromptSuite (see eval-suite-coverage.csv), class-based precision/recall thresholds for extraction tasks.
- Cost: per-token cost <= $0.0008 for gen traffic in steady state (post-batching recommendations).
- Reliability: >= 99.5% availability during business hours; automatic fallback to smaller variant if latency > 500ms for 2+ mins.

Exit gates (must all be satisfied):
1) Eval pass: CorePromptSuite weighted score >= 0.92 and no drop > 3% against baseline for critical intents.
2) Perf stability: 24-hour soak run with <5% latency variance and no tail latencies > 1s at 95th percentile.
3) Security & compliance: signed data processing addendum and SOC2 evidence uploaded to your portal.
4) Procurement: PO or signed order form executed (DocuSign link included in BL-MAP-v1).

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Automated run of CorePromptSuite with seed and RNG fixed to reproduce outputs.
- Latency sweep with 1, 3, 5 RPS and 64/256/512 token scenarios.
- Regression tests for top 20 customer prompts.

Proposed close timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): align MAP and owners; hand off eval suite.
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests; first eval run.
- Week 2: perf tuning, batching & quantization recommendations applied; soak run.
- Week 3: final eval, acceptance review, procurement sign-off.

I copied Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (solutions) to handle success criteria mapping and the test harness. Dev, I'll need one engineer from your side for integration during Week 1 — can you confirm availability?

Next actions:
- BlueLeaf: confirm owners and any additional prompts you want included in the CorePromptSuite (reply by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: we will upload MAP v1 and eval suite to the shared Drive and schedule a 30-min sync.

Regards,

Jonas Weber
Head of GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Chang <ben.chang@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

Thanks Jonas — this looks thorough. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock the MAP: 

1) Latency baseline: our internal SLA target is 150ms median for 256 tokens under 5 RPS. Can Redwood commit to the 180ms or should we adjust the MAP to include a staged optimization plan?
2) Cost: the $0.0008 per-token target looks achievable, but we need clarity on how batching and KV caching will be measured and attributed for billing.
3) Acceptance tests: we will add 12 production prompts (PII redacted) to your CorePromptSuite; will you run those behind a flag so we don't affect other evaluations?

Also, Ben will own procurement on our side. He can confirm the PO timeline after we verify the soak run.

Olivia
Director, Product
BlueLeaf Analytics

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

Olivia — quick answers and pragmatic adjustments below.

1) Latency: let's keep 180ms as the MAP target but include a stretch target of 150ms with a milestone in Week 3. The MAP will show both numbers and the concrete tuning steps (kernel/quantization + model variant routing) we plan to apply.
2) Cost attribution: we'll provide a usage report that splits tokens by request ID and shows caching hit rates; we'll include a sample billing reconciliation CSV and a recommended measurement method in the MAP.
3) Prompt suite: yes — we'll run BlueLeaf prompts behind a BlueLeaf-specific flag and show both combined and per-account reports. We will not expose your prompts to other customers.

I've attached eval-suite-coverage.csv with baseline pass rates and identified the 18 tests we consider critical for acceptance.

I'll lead the acceptance review on Day 21. Jonas — can you confirm the resource on Redwood's side for Week 1 integration?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 12:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

Adding technical acceptance details and pass criteria so everyone has a clear checklist.

Technical acceptance checklist (pass/fail):
- CorePromptSuite weighted score >= 0.92 (see attached) — automated run, seed locked.
- No regression > 3% on class-level F1 for extraction intents.
- 95th percentile latency < 420ms on the 5 RPS / 256-token sweep after batching applied.
- End-to-end throughput validated with customer traffic simulator: sustained 5 RPS for 4 hours with no errors, circuit-breaker behavior verified.
- Fallback behavior: documented policy and tested by simulating a model variant OOM.

I recommend including the following acceptance tests in the eval plan:
- Randomized A/B of model variants vs baseline for 10k prompts to measure accuracy drift.
- Token accounting reconciliation between BlueLeaf logs and Redwood billing to within 0.5%.
- Security: verify that no logs with customer PII are stored; run quick sampling audit for 1% of requests.

Dev — can you confirm an engineer for Week 1 (+ two 2-hour windows for integration)?

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

I can take Week 1 integration. Available Mon/Tue 9–11am PDT.

A couple of technical risks to call out now:
- If BlueLeaf's top 12 prompts contain very long context windows (>1024 tokens), we need up-front alignment on tokenization and a fallback plan — that impacts both latency and cost.
- We will tune batching aggressively, but that may temporarily increase tail latency during the tuning window; we'll schedule tuning windows overnight where possible.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the integration steps and upload to the shared Drive.

Thanks,

Dev Patel
Senior Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueleaf.ai>, Ben Chang <ben.chang@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: success metrics and close targets

Great — thanks everyone. Final confirmations and next steps below:

Confirmed:
- Week 1 integration owner: Dev Patel (Mon/Tue 9–11am PDT).
- Eval suite: BlueLeaf will send their 12 prompts by EOD Wed. Redwood will add them behind account flag.
- Acceptance criteria: use the combined checklist Karthik outlined; Marissa to run acceptance review on Day 21.

Deliverables Redwood commits to before Week 1:
- Upload MAP v1 and test harness to shared Drive (done).
- Provide sample billing reconciliation CSV and measurement guidance (Marissa).
- Short integration runbook and two 2-hour integration windows (Dev).

Procurement note: Ben, when you are ready we will share the order form (DocuSign). The MAP includes a staged discount tied to meeting the Week 3 stretch latency milestone (150ms).

I'll book a 30-minute sync for Monday 09:30 PDT to kickoff integration and confirm owners live.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth eval.

Jonas Weber
Head of GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference
